html:
SMTO-EXE-0006 — Invalid working directory

GUID: 7b2d1c63-0594-4f32-bf34-ea1531ff5ca4
Slug: invalid-working-directory
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to run a command inside a folder that doesn't exist, or isn't a folder, on the chosen computer. The command never started, so nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the folder path shown in the error message, then check on the computer running the Gateway that this folder exists. Create it or correct the path if it doesn't. A command can only start inside a folder that already exists on the computer where it runs.
  2. If every command on that Gateway fails this way, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit on it, fix or clear Terminal working directory, and select Save changes. A missing starting folder saved for the Gateway makes all of its commands fail; leaving it blank uses the Gateway's own work folder.
  3. If the folder came from your request, tell SMTO the correct folder in the conversation and ask it to continue. SMTO will then use the folder you name instead of the one that doesn't exist.

What success looks like

  • The command starts and shows its output in the task instead of this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up the Gateway; its default work folder may have been moved or deleted. Don't keep sending the same folder path; it will fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected the command before launch because its resolved working directory did not exist, was not a directory, or could not be resolved on the execution target.

What this means

  • Working-directory validation found that the target path did not exist or was not a directory before process launch or terminal/model setup. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Working-directory validation found that the target path did not exist or was not a directory before process launch or terminal/model setup.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the resolved target-local path and directory type under the captured Gateway and workspace.

How to fix it

  • Read the cwd in the failed-to-start receipt (error_kind=invalid_working_directory). Create the directory on the Gateway host or correct the requested cwd; if the default is wrong, fix the Gateway record's Terminal working directory (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Edit) or GATEWAY_WORKDIR, which relative paths resolve against.
  • Choose or create an existing directory on the selected target within the authorized workspace.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorized target directory exists and validates before launch.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
